metadata.note: The Knoxville and Ohio Railroad - Knoxville - Clinton - Coal Creek (Lake City) - Careyville (Caryville) - Jellico, 65.3 miles - in each operator's colour (Rule 4 splits sharing geometry): the Knoxville and Kentucky (1871 anchor), the Knoxville and Ohio (1872-1881), the East Tennessee, Virginia and Georgia (1881-1894) and the Southern Railway (1894-1951 [OPEN]). metadata.geometry_method: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror, cached degree tiles; opstrace.py): Dijkstra over all railway ways, ways tagged old_railway_operator=Southern costed 1x, untagged 1.25x, other named operators 12x; waypoints Knoxville Southern Terminal (hand-pinned) - Powell - Heiskell - Clinton - Lake City (ex-Coal Creek) - Caryville (Careyville) - Elk Valley - Newcomb - Jellico, snapped by the layered DP; Douglas-Peucker 8 m, then trim_reversals. The route is the NS 'Knoxville District Oakdale Line' from the Knoxville terminal to Clinton and the NS 'Knoxville District Jellico Line' from Clinton to Jellico, both old_railway_operator=Southern; a 0.4 km untagged/yard stub joins the Oakdale Line junction to the tracks beside the Southern Terminal so the line starts at the station and leaves north-west without doubling back.
metadata.louisville_through_cars_1883_1905: Louisville and Nashville through cars and Louisville - Knoxville through trains used this line 1883-1905 between Jellico and Knoxville, but in ETV&G (1883-1894) and Southern (1894-1905) trains under those companies' own numbers (1889 'To Louisville' in the ETV&G's Knoxville & Ohio Division list; 1899 Southern No. 11 Pullman 'Knoxville to Louisville via Jellico and L.&N.'). No source shows L&N trains or crews south of Jellico before the L&N's own LaFollette line opened Apr 3 1905, so that service is carried by the ETV&G and Southern features here. NOT changed in this layer: knoxville_early_railroads.geojson 'Louisville and Nashville: Louisville – Knoxville' (ln-louisville-corbin-knoxville) still draws an L&N 1883-1905 segment over an unlabelled ~55 mi straight Jellico - LaFollette - Knoxville chord, ~9-12 km east of this line, on a route that did not exist until 1905 - a separate defect to fix there.
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] end: Southern Railway Knoxville - Jellico (sou-knoxville-jellico) is drawn to 1951, the last CONFIRMED year (Feb 1952 Official Guide, schedule of Apr 29 1951). No source dates the last passenger/mixed train; probably 1951-1956. Leads: ICC / Tennessee PSC discontinuance dockets 1951-56, the Knoxville News-Sentinel, Fowler's branchline.uk Tennessee PDF (unreachable 2026-10-28). Also whether Knoxville - Clinton outlived Clinton - Jellico.
Knoxville and Kentucky 1871 is a one-year [ANCHOR]: 1869-1870 passenger use after the Coal Creek opening, and any passenger use of the first ten miles in 1861 or 1866-68, are unproven.
Knoxville and Ohio start 1872 is the first K&O-named schedule found; the company took over in Oct/Dec 1871.
Coal Creek - Careyville opened 1877 (Harrison); first passenger schedule found is Dec 1878.

Careyville - Jellico start: Harrison's Sep 1 1882 completion vs the Careyville tunnel repairs into May 1883 vs through trains Jun 4 1883 (secondary). Drawn from 1883; primary-only start would be 1884.
1906-1950 on the Southern rests on continuity between the 1905 and 1951 schedules; no intermediate timetable read.
Whether the L&N had trackage rights or ran its own trains south of Jellico before 1905.
All headways and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates or counts from single years (see each feature).
Alignment changes since the 1870s-80s (Careyville tunnel, Norris reservoir era) not checked; all eras drawn on the present NS alignment.
branches_deliberately_omitted: Southern Railway Jellico - Fonde, KY (Clear Fork line, built 1905): no positive passenger evidence in any year; the 1951 Guide's Table 29 prints 'Freight Service only.' directly after the Clinton - Jellico mixed-train note (drawable: NONE).
Coal Creek and New River RR / New River Branch, Coal Creek - Cambria, 4.02 mi (1880-81): coal branch, no passenger evidence (Rule 1).

Coal Creek - Briceville - Slatestone / Minersville spurs and the Tennessee Valley Railway (Briceville - Panola), 1888-89: no timetable found; militia and special trains in the Coal Creek War of 1891-92 are not regular service (Rule 1).
Louisville - Knoxville through trains 1883-1905: not a separate feature; carried by the ETV&G and Southern features (see louisville_through_cars_1883_1905).
Southern Knoxville - Clinton - Harriman trains: they left this line at Clinton for the ETV&G-built Walden's Ridge line, which belongs to the ETV&G/Southern layers.
freight_only_excluded: Jellico - Fonde (Southern), New River Branch, Briceville spurs - see branches_deliberately_omitted. Nothing was trimmed on the main line.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] One proven year only. The Knoxville Daily Chronicle's railroad column prints 'Knoxville and Kentucky Railroad. Leaves Knoxville for Coal Creek at 5 p.m. Arrives at Knoxville 10:30 a.m.' under President Joseph A. Mabry (Jan 14 and Jan 21 1871, p.3) and under President C. M. McGhee (Jul 20 1871, p.3) - one daily round trip, listed beside the ETV&G passenger trains; most likely a mixed train, which counts. Service certainly ran wider both ways - Harrison has the 31 miles to Coal Creek opened in 1869, and the first ten miles (to Copper Ridge) in operation early in 1861 until the war suspended them - but no other year is confirmed for passengers. Do not widen this anchor without a source. The road was sold under the State lien in autumn 1871 (sale confirmed Oct 30 1871) and the purchasers renamed it the Knoxville and Ohio on Dec 15 1871 - see the K&O feature. Headway: one daily round trip as printed in 1871.
sources: Segment-level: the 1871 year and the one daily round trip are the Knoxville Daily Chronicle schedules of Jan 21 and Jul 20 1871 (p.3); the 1869 opening and the 1871 sale are Harrison pp.~864-871. avg_speed_kmh is NOT sourced.

segments.note: Knoxville - Heiskell's - Clinton - Coal Creek (now Lake City / Rocky Top), 31 miles. The start is the first CONFIRMED K&O-named schedule, not the takeover: the Knoxville Daily Chronicle of Dec 19 1872 (p.3) prints 'KNOXVILLE AND OHIO R.R. Arrive at Knoxville, 11:30 a.m.; leaves, 5 p.m.' The company took over the Knoxville and Kentucky's road on Oct 30 / Dec 15 1871 (Harrison), and the K&K 1871 anchor covers the year before, so 1871 is not drawn in K&O colour. Harrison: no attempt was made to extend past Coal Creek until title vested in Dec 1875. The 1881 end is the operator change, NOT an end of service: the East Tennessee, Virginia and Georgia bought control in Jun 1881 (deed Jul 8 1881) and ran the line thereafter (see the ETV&G feature). Headway: one daily round trip as printed in 1872 and 1878; not counted for other years.
sources: Segment-level: the 1872 start is the Knoxville Daily Chronicle of Dec 19 1872 p.3; the 1881 operator change is Harrison pp.~871-876 (ETV&G control Jun 1881, deed Jul 8 1881). Headway is from the 1872/1878 schedules only.

segments.note: The seven-mile extension Coal Creek - Careyville (now Caryville). Harrison dates the opening to 1877, but the first CONFIRMED passenger schedule is Dec 1878, so the line starts at 1878: the Knoxville Daily Chronicle of Dec 13 1878 (p.3) prints 'Knoxville and Ohio Railroad. Leaves Knoxville 4.15 p.m. Arrives at Careyville 7.15 p.m. Leave Careyville 6.00 a.m. Arrive at Knoxville 10.20 a.m. Make connections with both day trains on the E.T.V.&G. R.R.' The Chronicle of Oct 12 1880 (p.4) has the K&O selling passenger tickets at one fare. Drawn as its own feature, not as a later segment of the Knoxville - Coal Creek feature, because a segment cannot carry its own geometry and would draw these 7 miles from 1872. The 1881 end is the ETV&G takeover, NOT an end of service. Headway: one daily round trip as printed in 1878.

segments.note: The K&O as the ETV&G's 'Knoxville and Ohio Division': Knoxville - Heiskell's - Clinton - Coal Creek - Careyville, 38 miles. The ETV&G bought control in Jun 1881 (deed Jul 8 1881) and, per Harrison, operated the line 'at all times thereafter' as part of its system - the 1885 decree voiding the deed, the 1886 reorganization of the ETV&G Railroad as the ETV&G Railway, the R&D lease of 1888 and the K&O-to-ETV&G lease of Oct 1888 - Aug 1890 did not change who ran the trains. Knoxville Daily Chronicle Sep 2 1881 p.4: a passenger-fare reduction 'affects all the lines of road in the control of the Cole system, including the Knoxville and Ohio and North Carolina divisions'. Full-line ETV&G timetables of 1884 and 1889 (see the Careyville - Jellico feature) list Knoxville - Careyville stations. The Southern Railway took possession Aug 1 1894. Headway: two trains each way daily (Nos. 35-38 in 1884; a Louisville train and a Jellico accommodation in 1889); not counted for 1881-1883.

segments.note: The extension Careyville - Buckeye - Elk Valley - Newcomb - Jellico, meeting the L&N's Knoxville Branch at Jellico on the Kentucky line. SOURCE CONFLICT on the start, recorded rather than resolved: Harrison has it 'completed to Jellico on September 1, 1882'; the Knoxville Daily Tribune of May 5 1883 has the fire-damaged Careyville tunnel still under repair, with a temporary zig-zag over the mountain, and through Louisville trains to follow; a Campbell County history (secondary) dates through Louisville - Knoxville trains to June 4 1883; the first PRIMARY full-line timetable is the Morristown Gazette of Jun 4 1884 (p.4: ETV&G Nos. 35-38 daily, Knoxville ... Careyville - Buckeye - Elk Valley - Newcomb - Jellico, 'AT JELLICO with Louisville and Nashville RR for Louisville'). Drawn from 1883 on the secondary date agreeing with the May 1883 primary; on primary sources alone the start would be 1884, and 1882 traffic beyond Careyville may have been construction/special trains only. Maryville Times Jul 10 1889 (p.5): 'Knoxville & Ohio Division: To Louisville 9:00 p.m.; Jellico Accommodation ...; From Louisville 7:30 a.m.' The Louisville through trains ran in ETV&G timetables under ETV&G numbers south of Jellico. Southern possession Aug 1 1894. Headway: two trains each way daily (1884, 1889).

segments.note: Knoxville (Southern Terminal) - Clinton - Coal Creek - Careyville - Elk Valley - Newcomb - Jellico, 65.3 miles, a Southern 'proprietary line' from Aug 1 1894 (Southern bought the ETV&G's pledged K&O majority stock; Harrison). Maryville Times Jan 21 1899 (p.5): 'No. 11 carries Pullman sleeping car Knoxville to Louisville via Jellico and L.&N.'; 'No. 12 from Jel[lico], Cin'ti and Louisville'; 'No. 4 from Jellico'; 'No. 3 for Coal Creek and Jellico' - a Southern Louisville through train plus a Jellico local. The Comet (Johnson City) Jun 1 1905 (p.4) still lists 'Louisville to Knoxville via L.&N. and Jellico'. The L&N's own Jellico - LaFollette - Knoxville line opened Apr 3 1905, after which the Louisville through business left this line; the split at 1905 marks that, not a break in service. Headway: two trains each way daily as counted in 1899.

[OPEN] END: passenger service is confirmed to 1951 by the Feb 1952 Official Guide - Table 29 'KNOXVILLE, CLINTON AND FONDE', dated April 29 1951: 'Passengers handled on daily, except Sunday, mixed trains, northbound, due to leave Clinton 8 15 a.m., arrive Jellico 11 00 a.m.; southbound, due to leave Jellico 7 30 a.m., arrive Clinton 11 30 a.m.', with its own Knoxville - Clinton times, and the index lists Jellico, Careyville, Newcomb, Elk Valley, Pioneer, Lake City, Anthras and Offutt as 'Southern, 29' without the freight-only dagger. 1951 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped (an uncited Wikipedia line says Knoxville's Southern locals were gone 'by 1956'). Do not extend without evidence. Also unknown whether Knoxville - Clinton outlived Clinton - Jellico. 1906-1950 rests on continuity between the confirmed 1905 and 1951 schedules; no intermediate timetable was read. Headway: one mixed train each way daily except Sunday, counted for 1951 only.
sources: Segment-level: the 1951 [OPEN] end is the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 29 (schedules of Apr 29 1951); the 1905 start of this segment is The Comet of Jun 1 1905 p.4 and the Apr 1905 L&N opening (tngenweb, secondary). 1906-1950 is NOT SOURCED year by year. Headway counted for 1951 only.
